title: Ecological Validity Assessment for Safety Benchmarks

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if benchmarks do not predict real-world safety behavior, the entire evaluation enterprise is misaligned. Directly addresses the evaluation gap identified in multiple safety reports.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Curating ecologically valid datasets requires careful judgment about what constitutes real-world misuse patterns. Comparing benchmark predictions requires model access and solid ML fundamentals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Collecting or curating real-world harmful request patterns plus comparing with benchmark predictions is sustained effort, though scoping to one benchmark and one source is possible.

novelty.reasoning: The 'sociotechnical gap' between benchmark evaluation and real-world deployment is well-documented. 'How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?' (arxiv 2601.23112, Jan 2026) directly discusses ecological validity of safety benchmarks. 'Can We Trust AI Benchmarks?' (arxiv 2502.06559) and 'Beyond Static AI Evaluations' (arxiv 2405.10632) address the construct validity and real-world prediction gap. While the problem is well-characterized, a systematic empirical comparison between benchmark predictions and real-world safety behavior using deployment data has not been published.
